textRun.content: Localization, mapping, and planning provide a strong foundation for collision-free motion.
VLAs connect semantic goals to motion
Pretrained visual and language knowledge can support navigation to new targets in unfamiliar scenes.
“Go to the person wearing the orange jacket” requires grounding language in visual observations.
Goal: reach the person wearing the orange jacket
Reaching a goal requires reliable obstacle avoidance.
Cluttered scenes expose failures in collision avoidance.
Open spaces expose failures in goal reaching.
Egocentric video as a source of navigation training data

textRun.content: Diverse real-world scenes, including clutter and crowds
Scalable source of navigation training data
No robot action labels or explicit navigation goals
Three stage pipeline to turn unlabeled video into navigation training data.
Estimate depth, align the ground plane, and build an ESDF.
Align text, image, and waypoint goals with the scene.
Plan obstacle-aware paths and refine them using the ESDF.
Future Work: Dynamic Worlds and Physics Simulation
Predict how people and moving objects respond to the robot, and plan through changing free space. (World Models)
Predict future 3D geometry and physical properties under candidate robot actions to evaluate motion before execution.
Optimize predicted paths directly on a TSDF so trajectories “flow” down the field’s energy landscape, without generating explicit action labels.
